A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BabyVLM-V2 and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched across model renaming, table relocation, and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, training and prompting ablations, and an 11-participant adult study in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental and adult-study outcomes and adds data-filtering and reasoning-budget experiments. The planned children's study remains prospective.

M1.justification: The reference model retains the LLaMA-1.1B backbone, ViT-L-16 encoder, MLP connector, objectives, and staged training procedure. BabyLLaVA-V2 is renamed "baby model"; the added larger-backbone experiment is a size ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both use SAYCam for pretraining and in-domain evaluation, Ego4D and original NIH Baby Toolbox stimuli for out-of-domain evaluation, and the same ten developmental tasks. Added ablations reuse existing coverage; revised sample counts do not establish new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds LLaVA-OneVision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, substantially broadening the main comparison to larger open-source models. The first two already appeared in v1's Figure 5 fine-tuning experiment, but were absent from its Table 4 comparison. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 7 revise instruction data from 150k to 113k examples and change several task-specific training/test counts. Appendix A.2 increases instruction-tuning learning rates tenfold: vision 1e-5 to 1e-4, language/connector 5e-5 to 5e-4. Added experiments introduce filtering controls, a doubled language-model size, and reasoning budgets from 0 to 25,000 tokens. These establish reported setting revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds preprocessing-filter ablations in D.3/Table 11, a reasoning-budget analysis in D.7/Figure 20, and a brief doubled-backbone experiment in A.1. Existing analyses remain, including the fine-tuning comparison moved from v1 Table 5 to v2 Table 12. Figure 20's second task is ambiguous: its legend says Subitize (Naturalistic), whereas D.7 says Who Has More (Naturalistic).

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance-test procedures. The added results retain point-estimate reporting; the new phrase "no significant gain" does not document a statistical test.

E6.justification: Reported reference-model accuracy changes from 55.2% to 63.9% in Table 4 and from 41.1% to 48.8% on Ego4D in Table 9. The fine-tuning ranking reverses: separate/mixed accuracy changes from 56.0/55.2 to 56.9/63.9. Synthetic-caption results and Figure 17 curves also change, with new baseline and ablation results added. These are revised results under changed reported settings, not controlled version-to-version gains.

T1.justification: The formal exit-region task definition in B.7 and the memory-task construction and dyad-based accuracy equations in B.8 are retained. No new theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: developmentally grounded multimodal pretraining, a compact model trained from scratch, and ten NIH-grounded evaluation tasks. The claim of outperforming GPT-4o on selected tasks is retained rather than newly introduced.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets filtering as beneficial, stricter filtering as a potential improvement, and extended reasoning as task-dependent rather than universally helpful. Appendix A.1 also uses the reported lack of benefit from a larger backbone to justify model size. Existing domain-generalization limitations and pending child validation remain.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly discloses validation-set counts, Figure 17 specifies that results are from epoch 1, and A.2 revises instruction-tuning time from 60 to approximately 24 hours. Hardware information is retained, and both PDFs still describe dataset, checkpoint, and script release as forthcoming.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added: LLaVA-OneVision, Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning, the GPT-5 system card, InternVL3.5, and the Qwen3 technical report. These support model attribution and comparison; the broader developmental-learning positioning remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consistently renames BabyLLaVA-V2 to "baby model", edits wording and headings, shortens Section 4.2 by moving its fine-tuning discussion into Appendix D, and adds an ethical-considerations appendix. Most narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11 and Figure 20, expands Table 4 with model-size groups, and adds validation counts to Table 3. The fine-tuning table moves to the appendix, the caption-source table moves earlier, and Figure 17 is redrawn with an expanded caption. Most figures and the two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Larger-model comparisons, filtering ablations, and additional setting disclosures strengthen the evaluation. However, v2 introduces material reporting conflicts: Section 4.4 retains 55.2%/41.1% despite Tables 4/9 reporting 63.9%/48.8%; D.4 favors separate tuning although Table 12 favors mixed tuning; and Figure 20 names a different task from D.7. These problems affect interpretation of revised and newly added evidence, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
